fact_label: Retiree/pensioner residence permit — financial requirement (funds-available bank certificate, NOT an income test)
value_raw: None — no income threshold exists for this route: the size of the applicant's own pension is not regulated. The financial gate is funds-available, evidenced by a Bulgarian bank certificate: 12 × the Bulgarian minimum monthly pension for the 1-year residence permit (€4,170.12 at the €347.51/month minimum pension in force from 1 Jul 2026), and 6 × (€2,085.06) at the preceding type-D visa stage. A stock held on deposit, not an annual flow.
unit: € available on deposit (12 × minimum monthly pension for a 1-year permit; 6 × at the visa stage) — a one-time balance, NOT €/year of income
date: 2026-07-11 (original); 2026-08-25 (recheck, [specialist]); 2026-08-26 (category-error remediation after [specialist] Return for revision, primary-law re-derivation, [specialist])
notes: CATEGORY ERROR CORRECTED 2026-08-26 ([specialist], remediating [specialist] Return for revision of the 2026-08-25 review, our records 2026-08-26). The 2026-08-25 pass encoded a bank-balance requirement as `unit: €/year` on a row labelled income threshold with model_target HardConstraintRule — a stock filed as a flow. Because our records' gate_amount() compares profile.income_monthly_usd against the threshold, that encoding would have passed a reader on income alone who holds no Bulgarian deposit, i.e. a false clear on the exact gate the row exists to close. value_num_low/high are now NULL so gate_amount() returns GAP_INSUFFICIENT_DATA (honest grey) rather than a false pass — same shape as the existing precedent TH:o-a-retirement-1-year-renewable-financial-requirement (bank-balance-or-income requirement, prose value_raw, NULL numerics). WHAT PRIMARY LAW ACTUALLY SAYS: the route is Чл. 24, ал. 1, т. 10 ЗЧРБ — the Bulgarian MFA's own type-D document page (https://www.mfa.bg/bg/5686, fetched 2026-08-26) states the ground as 'пенсионно осигурени и разполагат с достатъчно средства за издръжка в страната', and the pensioner-specific document it names is a Bulgarian bank document certifying an account exists to receive the pension transfers — with NO amount attached to the pensioner ground itself. The amount comes from the general sufficiency clause, which the MFA page, the Council of Ministers' administrative-services register (https://iisda.government.bg/adm_services/services/service_provision/21815, service 'Разрешаване на продължително пребиваване на чужденци', fetched twice with independently-worded prompts 2026-08-26) and MVR's own migration page all render as means of subsistence 'в размер, не по-малък от минималната месечна работна заплата, минималната стипендия или минималната пенсия за страната, за срока на пребиваване' — i.e. a per-month benchmark multiplied by the months of residence, which is where '12×' comes from for a 1-year permit and '6×' for the 6-month type-D visa. WHY IT IS A BALANCE, NOT INCOME: MVR's migration page states the evidence vehicle as 'Документ от българска банка за наличие на средства за издръжка в размер не по-малък от...' (funds PRESENT in a Bulgarian bank), and Bulgarian practitioners state the point explicitly. legex.bg (https://legex.bg/en/resisdence-for-pensioners), verbatim-confirmed across two independently-worded fetches 2026-08-26: 'The amount of the pension is not regulated, but the amount in a Bulgarian bank account must be equal to 12 minimum pensions according to Bulgarian legislation.' The previously-cited bulgarianexpert.com (https://bulgarianexpert.com/rp/rp-retirees-en.html) independently gives the same structure — 'at least 6 Bulgarian minimum pensions' for the visa and 'at least twelve Bulgarian minimum pensions' for the permit — but on stale 2020 figures (250 lev), and it states no income requirement at all; it is no longer the source_url because it does not contain the current value. blacksealaw.com (https://www.blacksealaw.com/bg/service/razreshenie-za-prebivavane-na-chuzhdenci---pensioneri) corroborates the same statutory formula in Bulgarian. THE MINIMUM-PENSION FIGURE (primary): Bulgaria's Ministry of Labour and Social Policy (https://www.mlsp.government.bg/ministr-efremova-s-promeni-v-udlzhitelniya-zakon-za-byudzheta-garantirame-che-ot-1-yuli-minimalnata-pensiya-za-stazh-i-vzra, published 2026-05-19): 'от 1 юли минималната пенсия за осигурителен стаж и възраст ще нарасне от 322,37 евро на 347,51 евро' (+7.8%, Swiss-rule indexation). So 12× = €4,170.12 today; it was €3,868.44 (12 × €322.37) between 1 Jan and 30 Jun 2026, and re-indexes every 1 July. RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY, NOT RESOLVED — WHICH BENCHMARK BINDS: the statutory clause is disjunctive (minimum wage OR minimum stipend OR minimum pension) and neither the MFA page, the iisda service record, nor the MVR page assigns one benchmark to the pensioner ground in its own words. Every practitioner source reads it as the minimum PENSION for this ground, which is why €4,170.12 is recorded. A stricter reading against the 2026 minimum WAGE (€620.20/month, ПМС № 243 of 13 Nov 2025) would give 12 × €620.20 = €7,442.40 — ~78% higher. Confidence stays Medium for exactly this reason: the mechanism and its shape are primary-sourced and certain; the multiplicand is practitioner-consensus, not primary-assigned. Anyone planning against this should budget for the wage-benchmark reading. DIVERGENCE (Confirmed-diverges): the statute's own words are flow-shaped — 'стабилни, редовни, предвидими и достатъчни средства за издръжка' (stable, regular, foreseeable and sufficient means) — while administrative practice tests a stock and expressly does not regulate the pension's size. A retiree with a large, regular pension and no Bulgarian deposit satisfies the statute's wording and fails the counter; a retiree with a small pension and €4,170.12 parked in a Bulgarian account passes. SUPERSEDED FIGURES PRESERVED: the 2026-07-11 original said '€6,000/year (~€500/month)', which conflated the minimum WAGE with the minimum PENSION (that diagnosis, from 2026-08-25, was correct and is unchanged). The 2026-08-25 replacement said '€3,864-4,164/year' — numerically close to the 12× figure but wrong in kind, and it is the kind that broke the gate. Neither is reinstated.

value_raw: AT, BE, CY, CZ, DE, DK, EE, ES, FI, FR, GR, HR, HU, IE, IS, IT, LI, LT, LU, LV, MT, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SE, SI, SK
date: 2004-04-29 (Directive 2004/38/EC adopted; transposition deadline 2006-04-30; consolidated text current through amending Directive 2011/24/EU, in force 2011-06-16)
document_conditional_note: Residence beyond three months requires meeting one of several conditions (Directive 2004/38/EC Art. 7): being a worker or self-employed, having sufficient resources plus comprehensive health insurance, being an enrolled student with resources and insurance, or being a qualifying family member of someone who meets one of those. This is an additional, better-secured right some readers can go on to claim -- it is never a condition on the entry/short-stay tier shown above, which is already unconditionally true for up to three months under Art. 6 ("without any conditions or any formalities other than the requirement to hold a valid identity card or passport"). A host state may ask for registration after arrival (Art. 8), but the Directive states plainly that holding a registration certificate "may under no circumstances be made a precondition for the exercise of a right" -- a formality, not a gate.
notes: Verified directly against Directive 2004/38/EC's consolidated text (EUR-Lex, CELEX:02004L0038-20110616, fetched directly 2026-07-21, primary-source-recheck) -- [specialist]-keyed, priority coverage build-out. Every other EU/EEA member-state nationality holds a treaty right of free movement and residence in Bulgaria under this Directive -- confirmed operative text: Art. 5 (no entry visa/formality for a Union citizen with valid ID/passport), Art. 6 (residence up to 3 months unconditional), Art. 7 (residence beyond 3 months conditional on worker/self-employed/sufficient-resources-plus-insurance/student/family-member status), Art. 8 (post-arrival registration is a formality, never a precondition). BG is excluded from this row's own membership list -- a Bulgarian national is already home, not a foreign national entering Bulgaria, not a foreign national needing this treaty right to enter/reside in Bulgaria. **Tier-shape judgment call, named plainly:** an early framing described this as a conservative-default-plus-conditional-relief shape; re-deriving from the Directive's own text directly, that reading doesn't hold -- `exempt` is the reader's actual, unconditional entry/short-stay tier regardless of whether Art. 7's conditions are ever met (Art. 6 carries no condition at all), and the note discloses an ADDITIONAL, better-secured right (indefinite residence) some readers can reach on top of it -- the same shape as Mexico's/Argentina's third-country-visa facilities, not the MX-SAE/CR-PT-biometric shape where the headline tier itself is the fallback a reader gets absent the condition. Checked directly against the Directive's own text before settling on this reading. **Switzerland named and left in debt, not rounded up:** Swiss nationals move under a separate 1999 EU-Switzerland Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons, not this Directive -- two primary-tier fetch attempts (eda.admin.ch, ec.europa.eu) both failed to resolve (403/404, the same gov-domain fetch-blocking pattern this project has hit before), so CH's own standing ships unverified and absent from this bloc tonight, owed as a follow-up primary-source-recheck rather than assumed symmetric. Sibling rows: ES/PT/CR/BG each carry their own independently-derived version of this same finding (this project's own inherited-claims discipline -- not copied across unverified).

notes: Held-source extraction (2026-08-08 max_duration pass, [specialist]), from the file's own 2026-07-21 primary-source-recheck (Directive 2004/38/EC).
